text:
kevin.m: Quick sync — we need to pick a shape for the internal edge that fronts model-serving. REST JSON passthrough vs gRPC+protobuf native. Tradeoffs: observability, telemetry propagation, quotas, and graceful fallback when a model variant is down.
sara: I lean gRPC native for inter-service a11y. Strong typing, no re-serialization, faster for binary payloads. But the client surface (web/mobile) still wants JSON -> need a gateway layer anyway.
alex: +1 for gRPC internally. But important: we must centralize quota enforcement and token-level cost attribution at the edge. That suggests a thin gateway doing auth/quotas/telemetry, not heavy rework of protobufs.
jamie: Concern: gRPC prevents easy canarying across heterogeneous clients. If we do proto-only, how do we route old clients? We could use a gateway header to pin rollout versions.
kevin.m: Agreed. Proposal A: gRPC between services, envoy-based gateway that exposes both REST and gRPC, translates JSON<->proto, injects headers: x-rw-client, x-rollout, x-quota-key. The gateway also emits request/response size, downstream model id, latency, and per-route token-estimate metric.
maria: Proposal B: Keep REST as canonical internal surface (JSON) to reduce translation layers. Use protobufs only for payload contracts between the runtime and model workers. Pros: simpler for product teams to operate. Cons: double-serialization on runtime path.
andrew: We should quantify CPU cost of JSON<->proto conversions. On our p3 nodes that will eat cycles on critical path. If conversion costs >2% of p99 tail, that favors proto-native.
alex: We ran a small benchmark earlier. Rough snippet:
```
# synthetic benchmark: 1M small requests
json->proto conversion cost ~ 12us/op
gRPC wallcall overhead ~ 4us/op
end-to-end additional CPU ~ 16us/op
```
That added ~8% CPU at our target QPS.
jamie: Can we mitigate with a hybrid: proto on high-throughput routes (generation/embeddings) and REST for low-throughput admin/control endpoints? That would reduce pressure while keeping ergonomics.
kevin.m: Hybrid seems pragmatic. Key non-functional requirements: 1) telemetry: must carry trace id and token accounting; 2) quotas: enforce at the edge with fallback to rate-limit vs queue; 3) rollouts: header-based pinning + canary percentage; 4) graceful fallback: edge should route to cheaper/compatible model variant if primary fails.
infra-bot: deploy-check: gateway image build passed for proto-gateway branch. ci/edge-tests: 42/45 green, 3 flaky tests failing on streaming path.
sara: For telemetry, we need per-token counters emitted to metrics backend (prom + histograms). Suggest adding a small token-estimate header and an event on long responses. Also enrich traces with model.version and quantization profile.
maria: About quotas: if enforcement is at edge, how do we handle dedicated/private deployments? Edge there might be inside customer VPC. We should expose a library that can enforce identical semantics when there is no central edge.
kevin.m: Good point — plan: edge is primary enforcement point in hosted. For Dedicated/Private, we'll provide a lightweight enforcement shim and a compatibility layer that emits the same telemetry schema to our console collector (or to a customer endpoint if requested).
andrew: Implementation detail: header propagation list -> [traceparent, x-rw-client, x-rw-rollout, x-rw-caller, x-rw-token-est]. Document that in the API gateway README.
alex: One sticky thing: streaming responses. JSON-transcoding of chunked streaming is messy. If we gateway-stream to downstream model over HTTP/2 gRPC, clients that expect event-streams need translation. That will be a source of complexity and flakiness.
jamie: So rule of thumb: support gRPC streaming end-to-end for high-throughput/low-latency streaming routes. For browser clients use server-sent events or websockets at the edge which map to gRPC streams internally.
kevin.m: Action items:
- kevin.m: write RFC for Hybrid model (proto-native for model IO + REST for admin), include routing policy for canary header and percent-based rollout. (due: Tue)
- alex: run a 24h CPU/latency experiment with proto vs JSON conversion at realistic QPS and attach numbers. (due: Fri)
- sara: draft telemetry schema (token counters, model.version, quant profile, route) and an example prom job. (due: Wed)
- jamie: prototype envoy config for JSON<->gRPC transcoding and streaming fallback. Share config snippets here.
maria: FYI I want the RFC to include failure-mode flows (quota-exceeded, model-timeout, fallback-to-smaller-model). Those are critical for product SLAs.
kevin.m: Yep. I'll include an appendix for failure-mode diagrams and SLO impacts.
infra-bot: note: ticket INF-482 queued for gateway-canary infra automation.
alex: :thumbsup: sounds like a plan. If no objections by EOD I'll start the perf run.
kevin.m: Thanks all. Keeping the gateway thin and deterministic + proto-native where it matters is the current leaning. Will post the RFC link when ready.
